instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company runs a short-lived high performance computing (HPC) simulation on Amazon EC2 Linux instances for two weeks. The input data is in an Amazon S3 bucket, and the results must be written back to the bucket. The simulation needs a file system with very high throughput. If a file server fails, the job can read the input from Amazon S3 again and repeat the failed step. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an FSx for Lustre scratch file system linked to the bucket, and export the results to the bucket when the job ends.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an Amazon EFS Regional file system with Provisioned throughput, and copy the input data from the bucket before the job starts.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an FSx for Lustre scratch file system linked to the bucket, and turn on daily automatic backups to protect the results.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an FSx for Lustre persistent file system linked to the bucket, and turn on daily automatic backups of the file system.

items.stem: A research team trains machine learning models on a 200 TB dataset that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The training runs on a cluster of Linux GPU instances that needs a shared file system with very high throughput. Each training job reads only part of the dataset, and training must start as soon as possible after the cluster launches. Trained models must be stored in the bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an Amazon EFS file system, copy the dataset into it with an AWS DataSync task, and mount the file system on every GPU instance in the cluster.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that is linked to the bucket, start training at once, and export the trained models to the bucket.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system, copy the whole dataset into it with an AWS DataSync task, and start training after the copy completes.

options.label: D
options.text: Download the part of the dataset that each job needs from the bucket to an Amazon EBS volume on every GPU instance when the instance boots.

items.stem: A company runs on-premises ZFS file servers that Linux applications access over NFS. Several times each day, test teams create writable copies of production volumes from ZFS snapshots, and scripts automate this workflow. The company wants to migrate the file servers to AWS without changing the application code or the way the teams create these copies. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to an Amazon S3 bucket, and copy a production folder to a new directory each time a team needs a copy.

options.label: B
options.text: Migrate the data to Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, and create a writable clone volume from a point-in-time snapshot each time a team needs a copy.

options.label: C
options.text: Migrate the data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with NetApp SnapMirror, and create a volume from a SnapMirror copy each time a team needs a copy.

options.label: D
options.text: Migrate the data to Amazon EFS, back up the file system with AWS Backup, and restore a recovery point to a new file system each time a team needs a copy.
